design:rework-radar.name: Rework Radar
design:rework-radar.principle: Keep the five rework precursors — unverified edits, failing calls, corrections/steers, same-file churn, and memory loss (cold cache, drifted constraints, compaction) — on screen as six small counters, and let exactly one nudge speak only when a counter crosses a corpus-derived line, naming the keystroke or typed line that resets that counter, so the nudge retires by itself the moment the counter drops.

Rendering notes: every line verified at exactly 56 cells. Title in the top border like the dashboard header (`┌─Radar ── <session> ── <model> · turn N ┐`), sub-section titles in the `├─name───┤` rule lines, bottom border carries the key hints exactly as the dashboard footer does. Colour only for state: the amber tile is `edits 3 ✓never` (first edit >10 min or ≥14 calls ago with no verify), the red tile is `fails 2 ▸gh pr view` (consecutive non-denial errors ≥2; ≥3 fires the slot), `▸` marks the active nudge, dim for the `recent` log and the hint row. `≈` prefixes any estimated figure (`$.21/c` is shown as `≈$.21/c` when the shim is absent; `ctx` carries `est` without the shim). The state line uses tool-name phases only (IMPLEMENTING = Edit/Write/implement-class Bash; EXPLORING = Read/Grep/Glob/explore-class Bash) and quotes verify literally (`ran cargo test ok 12s ago`) rather than an inferred VERIFYING word; during API calls 1–5 of a run it appends `▸ steer window`, and when a silent_turn_reminder attachment landed it becomes `silent 3m50s · 18 calls · nudged 2×`. `render.rs ×5` appears in the state line when one file was edited ≥4× this turn (churn). The `soon` rule shows at most one line: the next-ranked NEXT nudge and the condition that will fire it, never a list. `recent` is a plain fact log (steer, fail, denied, commit, verify, churn, prompt, cache, acted/expired/snoozed) so the person sees why a nudge appeared or vanished; at heights <20 it is the first section to shrink, then `soon`.

Idle semantics: the `now` slot is empty and dim ("quiet — <the last verify and commit facts>"), followed by the session's retirement tally so the person can see the coach acted-and-vanished rather than went silent. Tiles keep their last values; `uncommit` flips to `clean · commit 3m` (hidden entirely outside a git repo); `cache warm 58m` is the only time figure shown while >5 min remain (the mm:ss countdown and the `cache cold in …` nudge only appear at ≤5 min on a 1 h TTL, ≤2 min on 5 m). `run —` because no turn is running. In WAITING (Claude asked a question) the state line becomes `WAITING 4m · Claude asked a question (2 options)` and the slot holds the reply nudge. In a bot loop (Ralph / workflow-driven, C058) the whole `now` block is replaced by the loop-health line `Stop hook re-fed the prompt 44x (~210 tok each)` and no human-facing nudge is queued.
always_on_numbers: edits N ✓age — edits since the last verify-class call plus the age of that call (`✓never` when none this turn; amber after 10 min or 14 calls since the first source edit). Why: the single biggest rework predictor in the corpus — 41% of source-edit turns (15/37) ended unverified and 13 of those stayed unverified next turn, while verified episodes reach a check in p50 2 calls / 31 s (C030 corrected, P01, P06). Doc-only edits (.md/.txt/.json/.yaml/.toml, 69% of edit turns) do not count.

run Nc +Nk (+ `▸ steer window` on calls 1–5, `silent 3m50s · nudged 2×` when the harness reminder fired) — API calls and context added since the last assistant text block. Why: the steer-now vs let-it-run decision: real interrupts cluster at p50 3 calls into a run (PH-14, session-phase summary) and 96% of >20-call runs end in text on their own, so an Esc later mostly wastes the cut turn (C023 corrected, C041 corrected). ctx delta comes from usage.input deltas already in State.

fails N ▸prefix / denied N — consecutive non-denial tool_result errors in the last 10 calls with the normalised 40-char command prefix of the last one; denials (toolDenialKind automode-blocked / permission-rule / user-rejected) are counted in a separate word because their fix is different (allow rule vs missing fact). Why: 5.1% of 4,333 Bash calls fail, 29 blind same-prefix retries/month of which 13 failed again, ~14 pure-error runs ≥3/month; 80 of 292 errors are policy denials that the old rule would have called 'retrying blind' (C037 corrected, C038 corrected, C050 corrected).

ctx Nk $x/c — context size and price per call at this context (subscribers: `ctx 412k · 5h 62%`; `(cold)` when the cache is not warm; `est`/≈ without the shim). Why: calls >300k are 25.5% of calls but 51.6% of spend ($0.18–0.31/call vs $0.06–0.07 <200k) and it grades the urgency of every boundary nudge (R10, R13): quiet <200k, visible 200–400k, insistent >400k (C005 corrected). Per-call price = ctx × cache_read from pricing.toml (fable-5-1 0.025×, so 4× weaker there).

cache warm 1h / cache cold 4:12 / cold 12m — prompt-cache state from the shim's prompt_cache.{warm, ttl, expires_at}; the mm:ss countdown replaces the TTL only when ≤5 min (1 h) or ≤2 min (5 m) remain; `—` without the shim, `≈` when derived from last_line_at_ms + agg.observed_ttl. Why: every gap >1 h in the corpus was cold (55/58, median re-cache 183k, up to 872k/$8), and a TTL flip 1h→5m is itself the 'over plan usage' signal (C001 corrected, C026 corrected, UNS-13, S02, C06).

uncommit +a −d · N files · Ne · Mm (mockup: `uncommit 18e · 42m`; `clean · commit 3m` when the tree is clean; hidden outside git) — uncommitted lines and files from `git diff --numstat HEAD` + `git status --porcelain` on the existing 5-s git tick, edit calls and minutes since HEAD last changed (`git rev-parse HEAD` / `git log -1 --format=%ct`, so commits made outside Claude Code reset it too). Why: it is the blast radius a rewind, a destructive Bash command or a bad commit puts at risk, and the tail (≥5 edits AND ≥30 min) is where the checkpoint habit lapses: median 7 min / 2 edits between commits, p75 34 min / 5 edits (C032 corrected, C044, C045, P31).
design:rework-radar.nudge_model: Engine: every radar rule is a pure predicate over State (as A01–A18 are today) but the Advice struct gains urgency, since_turn, window_turns, retires_on, acted (C062 corrected, C064). Three classes, strict pre-emption NOW > NEXT > LATER; within a class rank by expected rework avoided = prior(rework | signal) × cost of one correction turn (median $0.49, p90 $3.47 plus ~4.5 min per wrong direction, C030/C033 evidence), with fixed priors from the corpus and first_fired-newest as the tie-break. Fixed order within class: NOW = R05 turn died > R04 waiting > R01 fail cascade > R02 denial streak > R03 correction streak > R09 commit without check > R06 destructive git > R07 stacked steers; NEXT = R11 cold resume > R08 no check > R10 checkpoint > R12 post-compaction > R21 loop armed > R16 cache countdown > R17 switch window > R14 review before merge > R13 drift > R15 plan first (dim); LATER = R18 churn > R19 subagent ctx > R22 cache miss > R20 screenshots. Exactly one primary nudge (≤2 lines × 56 chars, the verb truncates so TUI, pane and skill render identically) plus at most one `soon` line = the next-ranked NEXT nudge with the condition that fires it; the person never triages a list (the full ranked/suppressed list exists only in `cctop query coach` and the MCP tool for the cctop-insights skill). Promotion: a nudge takes the slot only when its class beats the current one or the current one retired. Retirement, in order: (a) predicate false (the tile the nudge cites dropped below its line — this is why the tiles exist); (b) acted, one concrete observable per rule (R08: a Bash command matching the test/lint/build patterns or a Read of a file edited this turn; R01: a non-error result for that prefix; R02: a successful call with that prefix or the rule appearing in permissions.allow; R03/R18: the next typed prompt (a rewind leaves no marker); R04: the next user line or PostToolUse for the pending call; R10/R11: a new transcript file (/clear) or a /compact boundary; R14: a review marker or merge; R17: the next assistant line; R16: expires_at passing or a new assistant line); (c) hard TTL: NOW dies at turn end (turn_duration), NEXT at the next human prompt, LATER after 3 turns. Cooldown 5 turns per rule (R03 10 turns); 'shown' counts once per human turn in which the nudge held the slot, and a nudge shown 3 turns unacted self-snoozes for the session (Claude Code's own cooldownSessions tip pattern); `x` snoozes 5 turns, `X` for the session; all of it persisted to ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json with the TUI as the single writer when running (CLI/MCP/pane poller read-only, else write) so the 2-s poller never races the TUI and query/pane/skill show the same nudge with the same since_turn. Budget: max 1 new nudge per human turn (~760 turns/month → ≤760 lines/month vs 18 rules × every tick today), budget expressed in turns, not wall-clock, so long unattended turns do not starve it; toasts only for NOW, max 1 per turn, 4 s. Suppression: session_mode=loop (last 2 stop_hook_summary with hookErrors non-empty or a hook_blocking_error with hookEvent Stop in the last 3 turns and no typed prompt since — C058 corrected: bridge-session/entrypoint are NOT loop markers) replaces the slot with the loop-health line and queues nothing; session_mode=machine (last prompt promptSource system/sdk or origin.kind task-notification) and team sessions (agent-setting / stop_hook_summary.teamName) drop all 'reply with…' wording; subagent transcripts never feed the slot; the first 2 human turns and away >2 h suppress NEXT/LATER only — NOW alerts (R05 spend-limit hits land on the first call of a session in 13/14 cases, R01, R02, R03) and the return nudge R11 are exempt. Turn identity for every counter uses promptId + promptSource ∈ {typed, suggestion_accepted, queued} or origin.kind human (C057 corrected; the current heuristic over-counts prompts by 20%); isApiErrorMessage lines and isCompactSummary lines are excluded from all counters (C017 corrected: 8/8 compaction 'detections' today are zero-usage error lines). Never duplicate Claude Code's own footer: no pre-compaction countdown (its '% until auto-compact' already exists; A06 gets the '/compact <focus> while warm' wording), no 'context low', no auto-continue-at-limit, no effort-downgrade dialog. How it avoids nagging: the evidence lives in the tiles, so a nudge can retire without repeating; only one voice at a time; acted-detection means the line changes the moment the person does the thing; cooldown + self-snooze + persisted dismissals cap repeats; wrong-rate targets per rule ≤1 in 5 are enforced by the corrections (doc-only suppression for R08, denial exclusion for R01, structural-only markers for R03, commit as tie-breaker only for R10, plan exit removed from R17's cold list); anything static or config-shaped (prefix trim C010, never-invoked skills) stays out of this view and in the dashboard's Prefix overlay as a one-shot dismissible tip.

design:rework-radar.interaction: Toggle: global key `c` switches Dashboard ↔ Radar (the key the coach PRD US-009 already reserves for the second view; `r` is a free alternative), implemented as `State.view: View::{Dashboard, Radar}` checked at the top of App::draw so layout::solve is skipped (VIEW-01 pattern, not the panel-owned overlay); persisted in config.toml, `--view radar` / `cctop run --once --keys c` for headless snapshots, and added to BINDINGS so the help-overlay test covers it; Esc also returns to the dashboard. Inside Radar the view owns the keys first (like ledger_view::handle_key): `y` copies the nudge's typed line (the quoted reply, slash command or rule text) to the clipboard via pbcopy/xclip — a local action that never touches the session, so FR-15 read-only holds; there is no 'send to the session' key in the TUI. `x` snoozes the current nudge 5 turns (3rd snooze = rest of session), `X` dismisses it for the session; both write ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json so the pane, `cctop query coach` and the MCP tool show the same state. `Enter` opens the 'why' overlay (evidence lines with metric ids, the doc_key explanation, the acted predicate that will retire it, since_turn, and — read-only — the ranked list of suppressed/queued nudges with their reasons). `j`/`k` scroll the recent log, `l` toggles the log between facts and nudge lifecycle only, `?` help, `p` pause, `q` quit. Tiles are not focusable (nothing to do on them); pressing `1`–`6` on a tile opens the matching dashboard panel overlay (Files for edits/uncommit, Turn for run, Tools for fails, Context for ctx, Tokens for cache) and Esc comes back. In the function-hooks pane the same nudge carries digit hotkeys from an empty composer: `1` = $.prompt.fill({text}) puts the quoted line into the prompt box for the person to press Enter (never $.prompt.submit), `2` = snooze (writes the same advisor.json through $.process.run of `cctop query coach --snooze <id>`), `3` = why (opens the pane on the explanation). Width behaviour: at 40 columns the state line is ≤38 chars, tiles collapse to 2×3 at ≤12 chars each (`edit 3 ✓never`, `run 14c +38k`, `fail 2 ▸gh`, `ctx 412k`, `cache 1h`, `uncmt 18e 42m`), the nudge keeps its two 56-char lines wrapped, `soon` stays, `recent` drops; at height <20 `recent` shrinks first, then `soon`, and the slot never drops below 2 lines.
design:rework-radar.delivery_channels: One implementation, `cctop query coach` (C064): a pure function of State returning {state{word, run_len, elapsed_ms, waiting_on, churn_file}, numbers[edits_since_verify, last_verify_age_ms, run_calls, run_dctx, fails_consecutive, fail_prefix, denied, ctx, per_call_usd|limit_pct, cache{warm, ttl, expires_in_ms, recache_tokens}, uncommitted{add, del, files, edits, minutes}], nudge{id, urgency, line1, line2, typed_line, since_turn, retires_on, acted}, soon{id, text, fires_when}, recent[], suppressed[], session_mode}, every number with metric_id/approx like the other verbs, line1/line2 truncated to 56 by the verb; a Mode::Radar (or hidden-panel preset) in layout::solve; a `cctop_coach` MCP tool; the pane poller's known-verb list extended. Channels: (1) TUI Radar view (`c`): the full 56-column layout above — the only surface that shows the recent log. (2) Function-hooks pane (Overview → Radar section, declarative Box/Text tree from the JSON, polled every 2 s busy / 10 s idle via $.process.run): state line + 2×3 tiles + one nudge + one soon line at 40–50 columns; the AbovePrompt band (E21/S01) shows the nudge with digit Buttons 1 fill / 2 snooze / 3 why only for NOW and NEXT nudges that carry a typed line, and only while the composer is empty. (3) $.ui.status — the one-line reduction, rebuilt from the same JSON: `radar <STATE> · <the amber/red tiles only, max 2> · ▸ <nudge line1 clipped>` (e.g. `radar IMPLEMENTING · edit 3 ✓never · fail 2 ▸gh · ▸ 3 fails in a row: Esc + the missing fact`), plain `radar IDLE · clean · cache warm 58m` when quiet; one line per plugin, works below 110 columns and in the classic renderer. (4) $.ui.toast (4 s): NOW class only (R01, R02, R05, R06 when dirty, R07), max one per turn; NEXT/LATER never toast; R03 uses $.ui.log (a dim transcript row) instead because its evidence needs two lines. (5) $.ui.notice(tool_use_id, …) inside an open permission dialog for R02 only ('blocked 2× this turn — allow rule: Bash(gh api:*)'). (6) Desktop notification (alerts.rs critical() via osascript/notify-send, opt-in --notify): R04 waiting after 30 s (repeat once at 5 min of cache left) and R05 turn died — nothing else; it duplicates iTerm2's bell but adds value in tmux/Apple Terminal. (7) Events panel: every fired/acted/expired/snoozed nudge is an `events.note` row so the dashboard keeps the history without a second surface. (8) cctop-insights skill / cctop_coach MCP: answers 'what should I do now?' with nudge.line1/line2 + evidence, is the only place the suppressed list and the reasons ('R08 suppressed: doc-only edits') are exposed, and can apply a snooze; the skill shows the loop-health line and no nudge in bot loops. Version/availability gating shown as `—` per tile: cache and $/call need the status shim (prompt_cache ≥2.1.251), permission_pending/Stop.background_tasks/notification_type need `cctop install`, promptSource/promptId ≥2.1.220, diagnostics.cache_miss_reason ≥2.1.220; the JSON carries `source: {shim, hooks, transcript}` so each renderer can say why a tile is blank.
design:rework-radar.risks: (1) Classifier accuracy is the gate for the two most important nudges: the Bash phase classifier agrees with the model's own description on only 47–56% for verify (write+run commands), so R08/R09 depend on the C055 split (test vs build/lint, post-hoc confirmation from stdout) and a ~200-call hand-labelled sample before they escalate; until then ambiguous commands are labelled verify so the nudge errs to silence. (2) Wrong-rate: every rule targets ≤1 in 5 wrong fires and the corrections are what get it there (doc-only suppression 69% of edit turns for R08; denial exclusion for R01; structural-only markers for R03 — keyword detection is 90% false positive; commits as tie-breakers only for R10 — 19% boundary precision; plan exit removed from R17's cold list; task notifications excluded from idle turns); relax any of them and the coach becomes wallpaper. (3) Subscribers: $ figures are notional (all 8 status files carry rate_limits); tiles and nudges render tokens / limit share instead of $, and fable-5-1's 0.025× cache-read makes the ctx lever 4× weaker there. (4) Missing sources degrade tiles to `—`: without the shim there is no exact cache clock (fallback last call + observed TTL is labelled ≈); without `cctop install` there is no permission_pending, Stop.background_tasks, session_crons, notification_type or PreModelSwitch — R04 falls back to the transcript pending-question tracker, R10 to turn_duration only, R17 to history.jsonl; 0 of 42 local SessionStart events were resume/fork so R11's hook path is unverified. (5) Bot loops: without the C058 gate every 'reply with…' nudge fires into an empty terminal (one Ralph session re-fed 44×); the gate keys on stop_hook_summary.hookErrors / hook_blocking_error, not on bridge-session or entrypoint (those appear in interactive sessions too). (6) Persistence race: the pane poller spawns a fresh process every 2 s; advisor.json must have a single writer (the TUI when running) or since_turn/snooze state diverges across surfaces. (7) Phase words: IMPLEMENTING/EXPLORING come from tool names only; the 94% agreement figure is self-consistency with a rule labeler, not hand labels; a wrong state word is cosmetic but a wrong verify word would mis-time R08 — hence verify is quoted literally. (9) Timing honesty: R15 (plan first) and R17 (switch) fire after the call/command already started — they are undo windows costing one call; R14 fires after the push, before merge; queued prompts land at turn end 26/28 times, so R08 never promises mid-turn absorption. (10) Overlap with existing rules must be resolved, not layered: R01 subsumes A15, R11 replaces A02's timing, R22 replaces A01's heuristic, R10 replaces A18's timer, R19 replaces A14, R12's pre half becomes A06's wording; leaving both would double-fire. (11) Low-frequency rules (R12 one compaction in 113 sessions, R06 ~0.5/day, R03 3–8/month) are cheap when wrong but need fixtures the current session-a.jsonl cannot exercise: an 8+ call explore run, Edit→cargo test→commit, an unverified commit, an AskUserQuestion with a >1 h gap, a /clear (new file), TaskUpdate completed, a '<synthetic>' zero-usage line, a compact_boundary, a 3-fail run with and without denials, a Ralph loop stretch. (12) R18 (churn) is an addition supported only by the mining counts, not a verified candidate; it stays LATER and low in rank until verified. (13) Desktop notifications and the pane's AbovePrompt buttons are the only intrusive channels; both are opt-in and NOW-only, and the pane never submits a prompt (fill only), so the read-only stance (FR-15, pane PRD §6) is kept.

design:phase-coach.nudge_model:
PHASE DETECTOR (the substrate; C041 + scratchpad phases4.py coach_phase() + C055 classify_bash, agreement 5880/6255 = 94.0 % against the per-call rule labeler, zero-call latency in 93 % of segments — self-consistency, not hand labels, so VERIFY-dependent escalations stay gated on a ~200-call hand-label pass per C041/C055 corrections). Over the last ≤ 5 tool calls of the main transcript, Bash calls first classified by C055 (priority commit > implement > test | build/lint > ops > wait > gitread > explore; split on && ; |, cd/env stripped; 'X --check' = verify, plain formatter = implement; downgrade to 'unknown' when neither command nor result confirms a test). Then: last call commit-class or toolUseResult.gitOperation.commit → COMMIT; EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode/AskUserQuestion/TaskCreate or permission-mode plan → PLAN (+ WAITING while the tool_use has no tool_result); Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit or Bash implement → IMPLEMENT; test/build class → VERIFY, always rendered as the literal command + result age ('ran cargo test ok 12s ago') and never as an inferred word (Bash verify-vs-description agreement is only 47-56 %); read-only call → VERIFY if it is git status/diff after an implement in the previous 4 or a re-read of a just-edited path, IMPLEMENT if ≥ 2 implements in the previous 4, else EXPLORE with run length; Agent → EXPLORE (delegated); mcp__claude-in-chrome / Playwright → BROWSE; ssh/gh api/curl/kubectl/docker/clawctl → OPS; sleep/until → WAIT; no tool_use + text → ANSWERING; end_turn + ≥ 60 s with no user line → IDLE; AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode pending, Notification.notification_type in {idle_prompt, permission_prompt, agent_needs_input}, or PermissionRequest → WAITING; HAND-OFF is a synthetic phase entered when the C043 boundary predicate fires and held until the next human prompt. Turn identity uses promptId/promptSource/origin.kind (C057: human = typed|suggestion_accepted|queued, or origin.kind human when promptSource is absent; 'sdk' is its own loop-turn class), so machine turns never advance the phase clock. Lines with isApiErrorMessage or model '<synthetic>' never touch phase, context or velocity (C017/C060). Each phase carries a passive 'next:' default line (row 3) that is NOT a nudge and never counts against the budget: EXPLORE 'let it run · at 8 reads say: use an Explore subagent'; PLAN 'read the plan · ExitPlanMode keeps the cache warm'; IMPLEMENT 'let it run — a check lands ≤2 calls after edits'; VERIFY 'wait for the result · green → commit'; COMMIT/IDLE 'same task? keep typing · new? /rename → /clear'; WAITING 'reply now — one word is enough'; HAND-OFF 'ask for a 5-line note → /rename → /clear'.

SELECTION AND RANKING (C062 with its corrections). Every nudge declares urgency: NOW (act within this turn: interrupt, cascade, denial streak, waiting, destructive git, API error), NEXT (act at the next boundary: checkpoint, ctx cost, switch window, cold resume, drift, post-compaction), LATER (turn-end retrospectives: cache-miss cause, screenshots, prefix tip, agent counterfactual). NOW pre-empts NEXT pre-empts LATER. Within a class: (1) phase match — a nudge whose declared phases include the current phase outranks one that does not (the phase gate below already removes most mismatches); (2) token-calls saved = tokens × expected remaining calls, with remaining calls = the session's own p50 calls per long run (19), never 32; (3) recency (since_turn). Exactly one primary slot (rows 9-11: ▸ headline ≤ 52 chars, action line ≤ 52, evidence line ≤ 52 — the `cctop query coach` verb truncates, not the renderers, C064 correction) plus one NEXT line (rows 13-14) plus one 'soon' line (countdowns and the last cache/limit event, never advice). 'n' cycles the '1 of N' candidates in the slot. A nudge is promoted only when its class beats the current occupant or the occupant retired.

PHASE GATE (a nudge may only occupy a slot in the phases it names): N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE {EXPLORE}; N-PLAN-FEATURE {turn start, before any Edit}; N-CHECK {IMPLEMENT, IDLE at turn end} never {VERIFY}; N-CORRECTIONS {after turn end}; N-FAIL-CASCADE, N-DENIED, N-STEERS-STACKED, N-DESTRUCTIVE-GIT {any running turn}; N-COMMIT-GREEN {VERIFY→IDLE}; N-REVIEW-BEFORE-MERGE {COMMIT, IDLE}; N-CHECKPOINT, N-CTX-COST {IDLE/ANSWERING after a clean end_turn}; N-DRIFT {IDLE, WAITING — it asks for text in the next prompt}; N-POST-COMPACT {IDLE right after compact_boundary}; N-WAITING, N-CACHE-COUNTDOWN, N-COLD-RESUME {WAITING, IDLE}; N-SWITCH-WARM {the instant a /model|/fast row lands, any phase}; N-LOOP-ARM {when session_crons appears}; N-API-ERROR {any}; N-CACHE-MISS, N-SCREENSHOTS, N-AGENT-HEAVY, N-PREFIX-TIP {LATER: turn end or session start only}.

RETIREMENT: (a) predicate false; (b) acted — each nudge names one observable completion (Agent tool_use after N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE; a test/build-class Bash or a Read of a file edited this turn after N-CHECK; HEAD sha change or gitOperation.commit after N-COMMIT-GREEN; a new transcript file (/clear) or a Write to NOTES|PROGRESS|PLAN*.md after N-CHECKPOINT; promptSource typed after N-WAITING/N-CORRECTIONS; a successful call of the same prefix after N-FAIL-CASCADE/N-DENIED; Skill code-review|review|simplify|ultrareview or a review Agent after N-REVIEW-BEFORE-MERGE; expires_at passing or any assistant line after N-CACHE-COUNTDOWN); (c) hard TTL: NOW dies at turn end (turn_duration or Stop), NEXT at the next human prompt, LATER after 3 human turns. Acted vs retired is recorded (the idle mockup shows both) so a mis-detected 'acted' is visible.

RATE LIMITS AND ANTI-NAG: budget = max 1 newly promoted NEXT/LATER nudge per human turn (in turns, not wall-clock, so long unattended turns do not starve it); NOW-class edge events are exempt but each fires once per occurrence. Per-rule cooldown 5 human turns after retirement. 'Shown' counts once per human turn in which the nudge held the slot; a nudge shown 3 turns unacted self-snoozes for the session (Claude Code's tip cooldownSessions pattern, BIN strings). x = dismiss for the session, z = snooze 5 turns; both persist to ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json {rule, since_turn, shown, dismissed, snoozed_until_turn, acted_at} with a single writer (the TUI when running; CLI/MCP/pane read-only unless no TUI holds the file, C064 correction) so the pane's 2-s poller and the cctop-insights skill show the same nudge. Never duplicate Claude Code's own footer or dialogs: no context-low line, no auto-continue-at-limit line, no effort-downgrade dialog, no '/model warm confirm' (F16); the pre-compaction countdown is folded into A06's wording instead of a coach line (C018 correction). Wrong-rate bar: a nudge must have been right ≥ 4 in 5 in the corpus to take the ▸ slot; those that cannot (N-PLAN-FEATURE, 11 fires/month, unproven benefit) render as a dim NEXT line, and pure indicators (N-SILENT-RUN, N-STEERS strip token, loop health) never take a slot.

SUPPRESSION (C058 corrected): session_mode=loop when the last 2 stop_hook_summary lines have hookErrors non-empty (or a hook_blocking_error with hookEvent Stop in the last 3 turns) and no typed/suggestion_accepted prompt since → every 'reply with …' nudge is off and rows 9-11 show loop health ('Stop hook re-fed the prompt 44× (~210 tok each)'); session_mode=machine when the last prompt line is promptSource system/sdk or origin.kind task-notification; session_mode=team when agent-setting lines or stop_hook_summary.teamName exist (no /clear or reply advice; teammate messages are wanted). bridge-session, remote_session_change and entrypoint are NOT gates (they appear in ordinary sessions). First 2 human turns and away > 2 h suppress NEXT/LATER only; NOW alerts (API error — 13 of 14 rate-limit lines were spend-limit hits on a first call — interrupt, cascade, denial) are exempt. Subagent transcripts never feed nudges. Ralph/workflow sessions (hook_blocking_error, non-cctop Stop hook) never get N-CHECKPOINT, N-CHECK or N-REVIEW-BEFORE-MERGE.

DATA PREREQUISITES (all verified as present on disk or in the 2.1.269 types, none parsed today): C055 classifier with a 200-char Bash command kept in tools.calls and in the hook spool (tools.rs summarize_input clips to 30, hooks.rs:75 strips tool_input); C056 ingestion of toolUseResult (gitOperation, bashEditDiff, persistedOutputPath, staleReadFileStateHint, statusChange, AskUserQuestion answers), top-level toolDenialKind/userFeedback/interruptedMessageId/promptSource/origin, attachment subtypes (silent_turn_reminder, hook_blocking_error, queued_command, plan_mode(_exit), goal_status, auto_mode_exit, task_reminder), and the spooled Stop.background_tasks/session_crons/last_assistant_message, SessionStart.source, Notification.notification_type, PostToolUseFailure.is_interrupt (UNS-11/TASK-02); new hook subscriptions PostCompact, PermissionDenied, StopFailure, TaskCompleted, Pre/PostModelSwitch (H01); status.rs Sample extended with prompt_cache/effort/thinking/fast_mode (UNS-13); C017 synthetic filter + compact_boundary parse; C057 turn identity; GAP-01 recursive subagents/** scan; C032 git tick (numstat vs current HEAD, porcelain count, HEAD sha reset); Advice gains urgency/since_turn/retires_on/acted (C062) and `cctop query coach` + `cctop_coach` MCP tool + Mode::Coach (C064).

design:phase-coach.interaction:
SWITCHING: `c` toggles Dashboard ↔ Coach from anywhere (a global arm in App::handle_key before the '1'-'9' arm, added to BINDINGS so the help-overlay test and FR-11 stay green; persisted in Config like 'w', so the last view reopens); Esc in the coach view returns to the dashboard (matches 'clear focus / close overlay'); `L` (sessions), `t` (theme), `p` (pause), `+/-` (refresh) and `q` keep working. Implemented as `Mode::Coach` passed through layout::solve's existing `force: Option<Mode>` (C064 correction) rather than a panel-owned overlay (VIEW-01: overlays need an owning panel and close on Esc from any focused panel). Headless: `cctop run --once --keys c --size 56x20` renders it for insta snapshots at 40x24, 56x20 and 60x51 (LAYOUT-01: below 56 columns the two-tile rows stack to one tile per row and the evidence line is dropped first; at 40x24 the view is state line + 3 tiles + ▸ headline + action + footer).

INSIDE THE VIEW: `Enter` = act: the TUI is a separate read-only process with no channel into Claude Code, so Enter copies the nudge's exact action text (the queued prompt line, or the slash command such as `/compact focus on the failing test`) to the clipboard via pbcopy / xclip / wl-copy (fallback: a popup showing the text to select), marks the nudge 'acting' and waits for its acted-predicate (the idle mockup shows 'acted · cargo test ran 31 s later'); nothing is ever sent to the session from the TUI. In the pane, [1 act] calls `$.prompt.fill({ text })` (puts the text in the prompt box, the person presses Enter) or `$.prompt.suggest` (Tab to take) — never `$.prompt.submit` and never `$.command.run` (S01/A06); Buttons fire only while the pane is focused (ctrl+x tab). `x` = dismiss for the session; `z` = snooze 5 human turns; both persisted to ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json so `cctop query coach`, the MCP tool and the pane show the same state. `e` = why: opens the existing explain popup (rules::explain / `cctop query explain <nudge_id>`) with the evidence line expanded, the retire condition, the corpus rate ('right 10/10 in the last month' / 'fires ~15×/month') and the docs reference — every nudge's doc_key. `n` / `N` = cycle the '1 of N' candidates in the ▸ slot without dismissing. `$` = toggle tile 6 between turn and session cost. `?` = help lists these keys. Nothing in the coach view is scrollable: it is fixed at ≤ 20 rows so it fits a 40x24 terminal beside a session (LAYOUT-01 floor).

ONE-LINE REDUCTION (the same `cctop query coach` object rendered by every surface, truncated by the verb at 56 columns): `IMPL ✓never · ctx 412k · cache 41m · ▸ run cargo test` (≤ 56) / at 80: `IMPLEMENT ·3 files ✓never · ctx 412k $.21 · cache 41m · ▸ queue: run cargo test`. This line is what `$.ui.status` pins under the prompt and what the pane shows in inline placement (classic renderer) and below 50 body columns.
design:phase-coach.delivery_channels:
TUI coach view (this design; `Mode::Coach`): the full 20-row tree — the only surface with the numbers block, the NEXT line, the soon line and the acted/retired history; every nudge lands here; 1-s refresh ticks the clocks (cache countdown, silent-since-last-text, idle) locally because the status file only rewrites on Claude Code redraws (C001 verdict).

Function-hooks pane (`views/coach.tsx`, view bar hotkey 7, `/cctop coach`): renders the identical `cctop query coach` JSON (polled via $.process.run every 2 s busy / 10 s idle, US-004) as a Box/Text tree: header Text row (phase · turn · elapsed), a Box column of tiles — two-column rows at ≥ 60 body columns, one column below (US-005 rule), numbers right-aligned in fixed-width Boxes, every Text `wrap="truncate"`, colours by palette name only — then the ▸ nudge as three Text rows with a Button row `[1 act] [2 snooze] [3 dismiss] [4 why]` (hotkeys fire only when the pane is focused); `placement === "inline"` shows only the one-line reduction; engine-native fields override the binary's where both exist: `$.session.usage()` for context/limits, `turn.step` stop-chunk usage for the cache-miss toast the moment it happens (E03/S05), `tool.check` decision/rule for N-DENIED's exact rule (E05), `classic.PreModelSwitch` for N-SWITCH-WARM without cctop install (E12), `classic.SessionStart` resume fields for N-COLD-RESUME (E11), `classic.Stop.background_tasks/session_crons` for N-CHECKPOINT/N-LOOP-ARM (E15), `Spinner.mode` for the state word while a turn runs (E21). Snapshot-tested at 50 and 80 columns against a new fixture covering an 8-call explore run, Edit→cargo test→commit, an unverified commit, AskUserQuestion with a > 1 h gap, /clear, TaskUpdate completed and a '<synthetic>' zero-usage line (C064).

$.ui.status (always, one per plugin): the one-line reduction — phase word, 3 numbers, ▸ headline — so the coach exists at any width and in the classic renderer where the pane cannot dock (S01, S07); it never carries the action text (that is what Enter/[1 act] is for).

$.ui.toast (4 s, single slot): NOW-class edge events only, one per occurrence — cache miss with named cause (N-CACHE-MISS live from turn.step), fail cascade, denial streak, API error, destructive git, two stacked steers; never NEXT/LATER (checkpoint, drift, prefix, cost) which would be nagging in a transient bar. $.ui.notice(tool_use_id, …) annotates an open permission dialog with 'asked ×N — allow-rule: Bash(gh api:*)' (N-DENIED). $.prompt.fill / $.prompt.suggest are the pane's 'act' channel; $.ui.log records acted/retired lines dimly in the transcript view for the idle history.

Desktop notification (alerts.rs deliver()/critical() → osascript / notify-send, only with --notify, already opt-in): exactly three cases, because Claude Code's own channel gives no desktop toast in tmux/Apple Terminal but does in iTerm2 (C042 verdict): N-WAITING after 30 s (AskUserQuestion / Notification idle_prompt / permission_prompt / agent_needs_input only, never a '?' ending), repeated once when the cache clock reaches 5 min; N-CACHE-COUNTDOWN at T−5 (1h) / T−2 (5m) when the person has been idle ≥ 60 s; N-API-ERROR spend/session limit. Everything else stays on screen.

cctop-insights skill and MCP: a new `cctop_coach` MCP tool and `cctop query coach` (pure function of State like summary/ledger/advice, every number with metric_id/approx) answer 'what should I do right now' with {state, numbers, nudge{id, urgency, line1, line2, evidence, since_turn, retires_on, acted}, soon, suppressed[]}; the skill reads the same persisted advisor.json (read-only while the TUI runs) so it names the same nudge the pane shows, can explain it (`cctop query explain <id>`), and — the one write path outside the TUI — can offer to apply a CLAUDE.md line for N-DRIFT / repeated corrections only after the person says yes in the session (F19 pattern). The skill is also where session-level retrospectives go (agent counterfactual, screenshot habit, prefix tip) so the live view stays sparse.
design:phase-coach.risks:
1. Phase misclassification is the headline risk: the 94 % agreement is self-consistency against the same corpus's rule labeler, not hand labels, and Bash verify-vs-implement agreement with the model's own description is 47-56 % (C041/C055 verdicts). Mitigations built in: VERIFY is only ever the literal command + result age, IMPLEMENT/EXPLORE come from tool names, ambiguous write+run commands are labelled verify so verification nudges err to silence, and N-CHECK/N-COMMIT-GREEN escalation on the phase word is gated on a ~200-call hand-labelled sample before shipping; until then N-CHECK's turn-end trigger relies on tool names + the test/build regex only.

2. Data prerequisites are real work, not blockers, and nothing fires correctly without them: C055 classifier with the full Bash command (tools.rs clips to 30 chars; hooks.rs strips tool_input), C056/C057 ingestion (toolUseResult, toolDenialKind at the line top level, promptSource/origin, attachment subtypes, Stop payload), C017's synthetic-line filter (8 of 8 current 'compactions' are zero-usage error lines and '<synthetic>' is adopted as the model), UNS-13 prompt_cache parsing, GAP-01 recursive agent scan (66 % of workflow agents are failed '<synthetic>' spawns and must be excluded), C032's git tick rewrite (numstat vs current HEAD, not HEAD-at-attach), the Advice struct fields and persisted advisor.json (C062/C064). Shipping the view before these lands the old A01-A18 predicates in a new frame.

3. Source availability differs per install: without the status shim the cache tile is 'est' (last call + observed TTL) and the 5h tile is '—'; without `cctop install` there is no permission_pending, Stop.background_tasks, session_crons, PreModelSwitch or Notification type — N-WAITING then rests on AskUserQuestion pairing and the registry, N-CHECKPOINT on turn_duration only (pendingBackgroundAgentCount absent for 1/3 of turns and omitted when 0), N-SWITCH-WARM on history.jsonl. The view must render '—' rather than 0 and label estimates, or the numbers lie in exactly the sessions that need coaching.

4. Subscription vs API pricing: this owner is a subscriber (rate_limits present in all 8 status files), so every $ is notional; C005/C024 say render per-call cost as re-read tokens and limit share for subscribers, and the 5m-TTL flip on usage credits (C06) silently changes the countdown math mid-session — the design handles both but a wrong branch makes the cost tiles misleading.

5. Acted-predicate misfires (C062): an Agent spawned for another reason retires N-EXPLORE-DELEGATE, a Read of an edited file 'verifies' N-CHECK, a HEAD change from an outside commit retires N-COMMIT-GREEN. Mitigated by also retiring on predicate-false and by showing acted vs retired with the completion in the idle history so the person sees when the coach was fooled; the nudge count budget (1 new per human turn, ~6/h) bounds the damage.

6. Nagging in unattended sessions: Ralph loops, workflow-driven and team sessions would receive 'reply with …' advice into an empty terminal (44 hook_blocking_error lines in one session). The C058 gate uses the corrected loop signature (stop_hook_summary.hookErrors / hook_blocking_error, not promptSource system/sdk, not bridge-session/entrypoint) but a loop that ends between ticks re-enables nudges for one turn.

7. Volume is low and skewed: many nudges fire a handful of times a month (N-CORRECTIONS 3-8, N-COMMIT-GREEN top quartile, N-REVIEW-BEFORE-MERGE, N-POST-COMPACT once in 113 sessions, N-CACHE-COUNTDOWN 2-4 catches) while three sessions carry 83 % of the ctx-cost saving — the view may look empty most of the time (by design) and the owner may judge it idle; the idle mockup's history line is the answer, but it depends on the persisted advisor.json.

8. 1M-window behaviour: with one real compaction in 113 sessions and sessions running to 953k, the harness's own footer, A06 and CompactionSoon rarely engage; the coach deliberately does not duplicate them (C018 pre-half folded into A06), but a user who lowers /autocompact or runs a 200k model gets a different mix — thresholds must come from window − 13,000 honouring CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW / CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE (read via ps eww) or the countdown disagrees with Claude Code's footer.

9. Surface drift: three renderers (TUI, pane, skill) over one JSON only stay identical if the verb truncates line1/line2/evidence at 52-56 columns and the pane's 2-s poller never writes advisor.json while the TUI holds it (C064 correction); the existing insta snapshots (help overlay BINDINGS test, 40x24/60x51/122x37 layouts) need new cases and the footer text changes when `c` is added.

10. Claude Code moves under the design: transcript shapes are documented as internal and changing (sessions doc), prompt_cache/diagnostics/duration_ms are version-gated (2.1.220/251/260/267), silent_turn_reminder is model-capability gated, UserPromptSubmit.source 'may be omitted while the field rolls out', and tools_changed misses are already fixed in 2.1.267 — every trigger needs a version gate from the status line `version` and a graceful 'unobserved on this version' path, or the coach names causes that no longer exist.

design:traffic-light.name: Lights (cctop lights view: four state lights + one nudge slot)
design:traffic-light.principle: Four lights whose shape and colour you can read from the corner of your eye (○ quiet, ◐ watch, ● act), each tied to exactly one thing you can change (context size, cache warmth, limit pace, unverified/contested work), and a single nudge slot that only ever holds one NOW-beats-NEXT-beats-LATER action naming the exact keystroke, slash command or prompt line — everything else lives on the 9-panel dashboard.

Idle rules: all four glyphs are ○ and uncoloured (absence of colour is the signal, matching 'colours only for state'); the cache row shows coarse minutes only (the mm:ss countdown and the 'next' countdown are suppressed above 5 min — C001 correction: 'do not show the Soon countdown line at all when expires_at-now > 300 s'); the slot shows a dim 'nothing to do' line in the same style as the Advisor panel's 'no recommendation right now'; 'next' and 'snoozed' show '—'. Without the status-line shim, the cache row reads 'warm ≈55m (1h, from last call)' and the limits row reads '—' (limits are Option in State, C041 correction; S03).
always_on_numbers: 1. ctx tokens (context light, e.g. '412k'): the multiplier behind 66% of spend — every token added is re-read ~106× (context-cost-anatomy); exact from the shim's context_window (UNS-13/S01), else the transcript figure labelled 'est' as the Context panel does. Bands: ○ < 150k, ◐ 150–300k, ● ≥ 300k on 1M windows (C005 corrected: >300k = 51.6% of spend); on any window also ● when ctx ≥ (window − 13,000) − 20,000, the binary's own warn band (C017/BIN-01) — never a fixed 80%.

2. ≈$ per call at cache-read price (context light, e.g. '≈$0.21/call'): the one figure that makes 'continue vs /compact' decidable; = ctx × cache_read price for the current model from pricing.toml (fable-5-1 0.25 $/MTok, C005 correction) + median output × output price; shows '(cold)' when the cache is not warm (C041 correction) and keeps the ≈ because for this subscriber the dollars are notional rate-limit units (C005/C024).

3. cache warmth + time left (cache light, e.g. 'warm 41m (1h)' / 'cold in 4:12' / 'cold · 182k re-write'): the second lever (cold calls = 1.8% of calls, 14.6% of spend). From prompt_cache.{warm,ttl,expires_at,recache_tokens_if_cold} in ~/.cctop/status/<sid>.json (S02/F01, C001 verdict: the shim's TTL is right, trust it); fallback last_line_at_ms + agg.observed_ttl marked ≈; mm:ss only under 5 min; '—' before the first call.

4. 5h limit % + reset (limits light, e.g. '5h 62% · ↻ 2h10'): pacing for a subscriber; from rate_limits.five_hour (shim only; '—' when absent, S03); 7d shown in the same cell only when ≥ 60%; turns ◐ when the least-squares exhaustion time lands before resets_at (A13/ExhaustionBeforeReset, ALERT-01) and ● on a rate_limit/spend_limit error line (C060).

5. edits since last check + age of last check (rework light, e.g. 'edits 3 · ✓ none 11m' / 'edits 0 · ✓ 6m ago'): the verification-gap counter (C030 corrected: ~15 source-edit turns/month end unverified; P01 'give Claude a check it can run' is the top quality lever). Counts Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit on non-doc paths since the last test-class Bash call whose result confirmed a run (C055 corrected: test vs build/lint split, confirmed from stdout 'test result:'/'passed'/'failed', is_error for fail); doc-only edits (.md/.txt/.json/.yaml/.toml/.csv, 69% of edit turns) count 0. When a streak is active the cell is replaced by the streak ('3 fails', '2 corrections', '2 blocked').

6. run size (state line, e.g. 'run 18c +42k · silent 3m50s'): calls and context added since the last assistant text block, plus seconds since that text and the harness's own silent_turn_reminder count when present (C023 corrected: 34 reminders/month at 6/11/16/21 calls; long runs end in text 96%). It is the Esc-or-wait decision number (interrupts cluster at 3 calls in, PH-14) and is deliberately not a light — it is a state, not a problem.
design:traffic-light.nudge_model:
SUBSTRATE. `cctop query coach` (C064 corrected) is one pure function of State returning {state:{word, run_calls, run_dctx, silent_ms, waiting_on}, lights:[{id, level:0|1|2, number, detail}×4], nudge:{id, family, urgency, line1, line2, action_text, since_turn, retires_on, acted}, next:{id, text}, snoozed:[{id, until_turn}]}; the verb truncates line1/line2 to 56 chars (TUI clips to width−5 with '…') so TUI, pane and skill render identically. Advice (src/advisor/mod.rs:41-49) gains urgency, family, since_turn, retires_on, acted; Engine state persists to ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json with a single writer (TUI when running, else the CLI/MCP caller) so the 2 s pane poller never races the TUI.

LIGHTS ARE STATES, NOT MESSAGES. A light's level is a pure predicate re-evaluated every tick and never rate-limited; it cannot nag because it says nothing. Each nudge belongs to exactly one light and one family (context-reset, cache-warmth, cache-switch, limits, verify, correction, failure, denial, waiting, review, commit-tail, git-safety, agents, prefix, loop, drift, compaction). When a nudge is snoozed or retired its light keeps its level (C062: 'the strip numbers still show it'); so a red light with an empty slot means 'you told me to be quiet about this'.

ONE SLOT. Exactly one nudge is shown (headline row, action row, keys row); at most one 'next' row holds the highest-ranked nudge of the next-lower class; at most one 'snoozed' row lists what the person silenced. Classes (C062): NOW = act within this turn (waiting on you, cache cold in <5 min with a reply pending, warm /model undo window, failure cascade, denial streak, destructive git on a dirty tree, unverified source edits at turn end, API error / limit hit); NEXT = act at the next boundary (context checkpoint, cold resume, PR without review, commit tail, loop armed, post-compaction restate); LATER = turn-end retrospectives (diagnosed cache miss, screenshot-heavy turn, agent context, prefix tip, instruction drift, manual-compact-without-focus). NOW pre-empts NEXT pre-empts LATER; within a class rank by token-calls saved = tokens at stake × expected remaining calls, using the session's own p50 calls per long run (19, C005 correction — never a fixed 32); ties by recency (newest first, as RULE-ENGINE does today). Promotion happens only when the current occupant retires or a higher class arrives; a same-class newcomer waits in 'next'.

RETIREMENT (each nudge names all three): (a) predicate false; (b) acted — an observable completion: a test/build-class Bash call or a Read of a file edited this turn (verify), a new assistant line / API call (cache countdown, waiting, switch-undo), a new transcript file or SessionStart source=clear (checkpoint, cold resume), a successful call of the failing prefix (failure, denial), a review-marker Skill/Agent or PR merge (review), HEAD change (commit tail), the next human prompt (correction, git-safety, post-compaction); (c) hard TTL — NOW dies at turn end (turn_duration/Stop), NEXT at the next human prompt, LATER after 3 human turns. Human turn = promptSource ∈ {typed, suggestion_accepted, queued} or origin.kind == human (C057 corrected; the current heuristic over-counts 20%).

COOLDOWN AND SNOOZE. Per rule: 5 human turns after retirement (10 for correction streak, C035). A nudge that held the slot during 3 human turns without an acted event self-snoozes for the session (Claude Code's own tip cooldownSessions pattern, X01); 'shown' is counted once per human turn, not per render tick (C062 correction). x = snooze 5 turns, X = snooze for the session; both persist to the advisor.json so `cctop query coach`, the pane and the skill agree. Budget: at most 1 newly promoted nudge per human turn and at most 1 LATER promotion per 2 human turns (budgets in turns, not wall-clock, so an unattended 3-hour turn does not starve or flood it); a re-fire of the same family (context +100k steps) counts against the budget.

SUPPRESSION. session_mode (C058 corrected): loop when the last 2 stop_hook_summary lines have hookErrors non-empty or a hook_blocking_error with hookEvent==Stop appears in the last 3 turns and no typed prompt since → no 'reply with…' nudges at all, state line shows 'LOOP · stop hook re-fed prompt 44× (~210 tok each)'; machine when the last prompt is promptSource system / origin task-notification; team when agent-setting or teamName present (no cross-session-message advice). Also: subagent transcripts never feed nudges; NEXT/LATER are silent for the first 2 human turns and after > 2 h away (the cold-resume nudge is the one NEXT exception); NOW is exempt from both (13 of 14 rate-limit errors land on a session's first call, C062 correction). Never duplicate Claude Code's own footer: no pre-compaction countdown (harness shows '% until auto-compact', C018 verdict), no 'auto-continue at limit' echo, no effort-downgrade dialog echo, no 'queued message reads at next call' (C059 demoted to a state-line token). Never fire on <synthetic>/isApiErrorMessage lines for context, velocity or model (C017/C060) — those lines produce only the API-error nudge.

EVIDENCE NEXT TO ADVICE. Every nudge's numbers come from a light or the state line already on screen (the verify nudge cites the rework cell, the cache nudge cites the cache cell), so the person never has to trust a figure they cannot see; 'e' opens the explain overlay with the evidence, the metric ids and the doc_key, in the Advisor overlay style.

design:traffic-light.interaction:
TOGGLE. 'v' (global, free in BINDINGS/footer today: ?, 1-9, Tab, Esc, p, w, +, -, q, a, t, L are taken) flips Dashboard ↔ Lights; implemented as `pub view: View { Dashboard, Coach }` on State checked at the top of App::draw before layout::solve (VIEW-01's recommended pattern, not the panel-owned overlay), persisted in Config like layout/theme, settable with `cctop run --view lights` and `cctop run --once --keys v --size 56x20` for snapshot tests; added to BINDINGS so the help-overlay test (app.rs:832-847) and FR-11 stay green. The lights view has its own key handler like ledger_view::handle_key; global keys (?, p, +/-, q, a, t, L, Ctrl-C) keep working.

IN THE VIEW.
- Enter = act: copies the nudge's action_text (the quoted prompt line, the slash command, or the allow-rule string) to the clipboard via OSC 52 (works in tmux/iTerm/kitty/WezTerm), falling back to pbcopy/xclip/wl-copy, and toasts 'copied: run cargo test, fix failures'. cctop is read-only, so nothing is ever sent to Claude Code's socket; the person pastes and presses Enter in the Claude Code pane. When the nudge's action is a keystroke (Esc, Esc Esc, Shift+Tab) Enter copies nothing and toasts the key sequence instead.
- x = snooze this nudge 5 human turns; X = snooze it for the session (persisted to ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json so `cctop query coach`, the pane and the skill agree; the Advisor panel's dismissed set is merged with it). The light keeps its level.
- e = explain overlay (Advisor overlay style, Esc closes): evidence lines with metric ids, the acted predicate ('clears when a test-class Bash call succeeds'), the class and rank, the doc_key text, and the extra lines that do not fit the slot (rewind checkpoints C045, error-class breakdown C038, cache-miss counters C002, agents failed-spawn count C014).
- n / N = peek at the next / previous ranked nudge without promoting it (the slot returns to the ranked head on the next tick; a peeked nudge can be snoozed with x).
- 1-4 = focus a light: the slot area temporarily shows that light's 3-line detail (context: threshold, +Δ this run, prefix share; cache: hit ratio, misses with last cause, TTL source; limits: 7d, other live sessions, exhaustion fit; rework: last check command and result, uncommitted tail, error classes this turn); Esc or the same digit returns to the nudge.
- ? = help (BINDINGS), q / Ctrl-C = quit, a = ask (existing), p = pause (existing; the 'PAUSED +N' pill renders in the footer as today).
- Footer text (dim, ≤ 56): ' v dashboard  Enter copy  x snooze  e why  1-4 light  q'; toasts replace it for 3 s in warn colour exactly as draw_footer does now.

DISMISS/SNOOZE SEMANTICS. x never hides a light; a snoozed nudge is listed on the 'snoozed' row with its remaining turns so silence is visibly the person's choice; a nudge that held the slot 3 human turns unacted self-snoozes for the session and moves to that row automatically. Retired nudges do not reappear until their cooldown (5 turns; 10 for the correction streak) has passed and the predicate is true again.

PANE / SKILL. The function-hooks pane renders the same `cctop query coach` object (polled by plugin/hooks/poller.ts every 2 s busy / 10 s idle) as a Box(column) with Text(state line), four Text light rows, Text nudge line1/line2 and two Buttons: 'snooze' (runs `cctop query coach --snooze <id>` via $.process.run; the CLI writes advisor.json only when no TUI owns it) and 'why' (expands the explain text in place); optionally, off by default, a 'fill' Button calls $.prompt.fill({text: action_text}) — zero tokens, the person still presses Enter (A06/E08; the pane PRD forbids injection, not drafts). The cctop-insights skill answers 'why is the rework light red' from nudge.explain and may run the action only when the user asks.
design:traffic-light.delivery_channels:
1. TUI lights view (full-screen alternative, 'v'): the whole thing — state line, four lights, one slot, next/snoozed rows. Reason: the only surface with keys, colour and a persistent frame; the person keeps it in a side pane or tmux split (cctop:cctop skill) and reads it from the corner of the eye while typing in the Claude Code pane.

2. Function-hooks pane (declarative Box/Text tree, plugin/hooks/views): the same object via `cctop query coach` — verb added to poller.ts's known-verb list, `cctop_coach` MCP tool added to src/mcp.rs beside the 7 existing tools (C064). Lights rows use the same ○/◐/● glyphs with the color prop; below 50 columns the third figure of each light row is dropped and the nudge wraps; Spinner.mode (E21) may replace the transcript-derived phase word there. Snooze via a Button + `--snooze`; no digit hotkeys are needed. Reason: people who only run the plugin and never open the TUI still get the identical coaching; snapshot-tested at 50/80 cols with the existing tests/pane harness.

3. One-line status ($.ui.status, one per plugin; also usable as the cctop statusline-shim output line): reduction L0 (≥ 80 cols) '◐412k ≈$.21 · ○cache 41m · ○5h 62% · ●rework edits3 ✓none · ▸ queue: run cargo test, fix failures'; L1 (< 80) the four glyph+number pairs and a '▸' marker when a nudge is live; L2 the four glyphs only. It changes only when a light level or the slot occupant changes, never per tick, so it does not flicker. Reason: works at any width and in the classic renderer (S07, S01).

4. Toast ($.ui.toast 4 s in the pane; the 3 s footer toast in the TUI): only on promotion of a NOW-class nudge (waiting-on-you, cache cold in < 5 min with a reply pending, warm-switch undo, failure cascade, denial streak, destructive git, turn died) and only once per fire — never for NEXT/LATER, never on re-render, never for lights changing level. Reason: NOW is the only class where the value decays in minutes; C062's one-new-nudge-per-turn budget already caps the rate.

5. Desktop notification (alerts.rs critical() via osascript/notify-send, opt-in --notify): waiting-on-you after 30 s (AskUserQuestion / Notification idle_prompt|permission_prompt|agent_needs_input only, never a '?'), repeated once when the cache clock reaches 5 min; turn died (rate/spend limit, login expired); the existing ContextHigh/ExhaustionBeforeReset/McpExited criticals stay. Reason: Claude Code's own channel gives no desktop toast in tmux/Apple Terminal and its idle nudge fires at 75 min (after the 1 h TTL), so this is additive there and merely duplicative in iTerm2 — hence opt-in (C042 verdict).

6. cctop-insights skill / cctop_coach MCP tool: the same JSON plus explain text, for 'why is the cache light amber' and for letting Claude act on a nudge when the person asks ('do what the coach says'); the skill reads snoozed state so it never re-proposes a snoozed nudge. Reason: no third implementation; the skill is where a person turns a nudge into a CLAUDE.md line ('# rule', P27).

7. Events panel (dashboard view) and the SessionEnd report: every nudge fire, snooze and acted event is appended as an Events row ('coach verify-gap fired / acted (cargo test ok)') so the dashboard shows the audit trail and report.rs can list 'nudges: 7 fired, 4 acted, 2 snoozed' — the only way to tune the rules against real behaviour later.

Not used: `$.prompt.submit` and `$.tool.call` (a turn or a tool costs tokens and violates read-only); `additionalContext` injection into the model (pane PRD §6); Claude Code's own AbovePrompt band is reserved for a later optional 'hotkey buttons' variant (S01) once the TUI keys have been validated.
design:traffic-light.risks:
1. Verify vs implement classification is the weak link: the Bash phase classifier agrees with the model's own description only 47% for 'verify' (C055/C041 verdicts). Mitigation baked in: the rework light's ✓ resets only on a test-class command whose stdout confirms a run (or is_error), IMPLEMENTING/EXPLORING come from tool names only, and the ~200-call hand-labelled sample is a hard gate before the rework light may go red on the phase word; until then red comes only from structural events (cascade, corrections, denials, destructive git, turn-end edits with no test call at all).

2. Without the status-line shim two lights degrade: cache falls back to last call + observed TTL (marked ≈; wrong across a 1h→5m flip until the next call) and limits shows '—'; without `cctop install` hooks, permission_pending, Stop.background_tasks, session_crons and PreModelSwitch are absent, so waiting-on-you relies on transcript pairing and Notification lines, the checkpoint gate loses its 'no background work' check (turn_duration.pendingBackgroundAgentCount is omitted when 0 and missing for 1/3 of turns), and the warm-switch nudge becomes a post-hoc undo window from history.jsonl.

3. Dollar figures are notional for this subscriber (all status files carry rate_limits); ≈ and the limits light say so, but the /usage weighting (cached + uncached×10 + cacheCreate×12.5 + output×50 × model tier) is not reproduced, so '≈$0.21/call' can mislead about plan usage; a future 'limit units/call' variant needs that formula and the plan size.

4. Band thresholds (150k/300k on 1M windows, warn band window−13k−20k) are tuned on one month / 113 transcripts of one user; the effective auto-compact window can be lowered server-side (the one real compaction fired at 567k on a 1M model) so the context light must mirror Claude Code's own '% of window' when the window is not exact and never claim 'N turns until autocompact' (C017 correction).

5. Suppression depends on parsers that do not exist yet: session_mode (stop_hook_summary.hookErrors, hook_blocking_error, promptSource/origin.kind) and human-turn identity (C057; the current heuristic over-counts prompts 20%). Until C056/C057/C058 land, cooldowns count wrong turns and Ralph loops would receive 'reply with…' nudges into an empty terminal — the single fastest way to train the person to ignore the view.

6. One slot hides a second simultaneous problem; the lights and the 'next'/'+N' counter are the mitigation, but a person who never presses n or 1-4 sees only the top nudge. The ranking formula (tokens × remaining calls) systematically favours context/cache nudges over rework nudges of the same class; the class ordering (NOW first) is what keeps rework visible, and that ordering is a design choice, not measured.

7. Acted predicates can misfire (a test run for another reason retires the verify nudge; a new transcript file from an unrelated /clear retires the checkpoint) and cooldowns can hide a genuinely repeated problem; both are accepted because the light keeps its level and the Events audit trail records every fire/acted/snooze for later tuning.

8. Rendering: ○ ◐ ● ◆ ▸ ↻ ✓ are East-Asian-ambiguous-width glyphs (same class as the existing ◆ ■ ▸ ─ │ ·), so terminals set to ambiguous=wide will misalign rows — a theme-level ASCII fallback (o / + / * ) should exist as it does for the border set; OSC 52 clipboard is blocked in some terminals (Apple Terminal) so Enter must fall back to pbcopy/xclip and, failing that, show the text selectable in the explain overlay.

9. The persisted ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json introduces a writer race between the TUI and the 2 s pane poller / MCP callers; the single-writer rule (TUI owns the file while running; CLI writes only when no TUI lock exists) must be implemented with a lock file or the snooze state will flap.

10. Frequency claims come from a one-month, one-user corpus: cache-cold countdown realistically catches 2–4 events/month (C001 verdict), compaction restate ~1 per 113 sessions, warm-switch ~1 per 11 sessions; several nudges will be seen rarely, which is correct for a no-nag view but means the view's value is dominated by three families (verify gap, context reset, waiting-on-you) and the product should be judged on those.

11. Claude Code keeps moving: prompt_snapshot appears only on ≥ 2.1.266, diagnostics.cache_miss_reason on ≥ 2.1.220, silent_turn_reminder is model/version gated, tools_changed misses were fixed in 2.1.267; every parser must be version-gated on the transcript/status `version` field and the light must show '—' rather than a stale or invented value when its source is absent.

Idle rules: the cache tile shows minutes only (`warm 58m`) — the mm:ss countdown and the `soon` line appear only when < 5 min remain on a 1h TTL (< 2 min on 5m) per C001's correction, otherwise `soon —`. `next` keeps quoting the price of the next p50 run so the person sees that continuing is cheap right now (≈$1.0 vs $0.9 fresh) and no /clear is warranted. The `now` frame never invents advice: it states the comparison to the 7-day baseline and when the next evaluation happens (turn end), and offers `?` to review what was retired and why. Without the status shim the cache tile reads `cache ≈warm 1h` (from last_line_at_ms + agg.observed_ttl, UNS-10) and the 5h tile reads `5h —` (Limits is Option, C041 correction).
always_on_numbers: $/call ≈$0.23 @412k — the price of every step: context_size × cache-read price (+ median output tokens × output price) from State.agg.turns[].context_size and pricing.toml (fable-5-1 cache read 0.25 $/M = 0.025×, opus-5 0.5 $/M); valid only while prompt_cache.warm, else the tile reads `(cold: next call ≈$2.0)`. Why: calls above 300k are 25.5 % of calls but 51.6 % of spend, $/call 0.183–0.311 vs 0.056–0.074 below 200k (C005 verdict); this is the one number the person can move. `t` toggles the subscriber form `re-reads 412k/call` (C024: $ are notional on Pro/Max, all 8 status files carry rate_limits).

turn ≈$2.61 ×3.2 7d — this turn's priced usage so far (ledger.rs per-turn row, agents included when tokens_include_agents) versus the person's own 7-day median cost per turn (baseline.rs; BASE-01 says per-session medians exist and per-turn medians are a cheap addition in figures(); F25 stats-cache.json is the fallback). Why: 'vs your baseline' is the ticker's frame of reference — the top 5 % of turns (ctx p50 412k, 30 calls) are 40 % of spend, so a ×3 multiplier is the earliest honest warning that this turn is one of them.

design:cost-ticker.nudge_model: SELECTION. Every coach rule is a pure predicate over State (like A01–A18, RULE-ENGINE) that yields a Nudge {id, class, line1, line2, tokens_per_call_saved, remaining_calls_estimate, acted_predicate, retire_on, since_turn}. Class is fixed per rule: NOW (act within this turn: cache-miss just priced, denial streak, fail cascade, waiting-on-you, cache-clock under 5 min, turn died, running agent at ≥ 250k, no-check amber, destructive git), NEXT (act at the next boundary: cold-resume, ctx-price-checkpoint, switch undo window, idle-loop armed, post-compaction re-orientation, correction streak, review-before-merge, instruction drift), LATER (turn-end retrospectives: screenshots, prefix one-shot, agent fan-out, side-question /btw). RANKING. NOW pre-empts NEXT pre-empts LATER (C062); inside a class the key is priced saving = tokens_per_call_saved × remaining_calls_estimate × the model's cache-read price (or rate-limit weight fable 10 / opus 5 / sonnet 3 / haiku 1 when `t` shows limit units), where remaining_calls_estimate is the session's p50 calls per long run for NOW/NEXT and the 7-day median turns-per-session minus turns so far for LATER; ties go to the older since_turn. The title shows `1 of N` and `n`/`N` cycles the ranked list, but only the slot holder counts as 'shown'. EXACTLY ONE. One primary nudge (≤ 2 × 56 chars, truncated by the verb, not the renderer, C064) plus at most one `soon` line, which is always the highest-ranked NEXT nudge whose moment has not arrived (e.g. the ctx-price line armed for turn end while the turn runs). The slot changes only at a human-turn boundary or on a NOW event, never on a render tick, so the line does not flicker. RETIREMENT. (a) predicate false; (b) acted — each rule names an observable completion: a verify-class Bash call or a Read of an edited path (no-check), a new transcript file (/clear after checkpoint), an assistant line after the countdown (cache-clock), the next human prompt (correction streak), a successful call of the failing prefix (fail cascade), a review Skill/Agent marker (review-before-merge), prompt_cache.warm back to true (switch), SubagentStop (agent-ctx); (c) hard TTL: NOW dies at turn end (turn_duration/Stop), NEXT at the next human prompt (promptSource typed|suggestion_accepted|queued, C057), LATER after 3 human turns. RATE LIMITS. Cooldown 5 human turns per rule (10 for the correction streak); a nudge that held the slot for 3 human turns unacted self-snoozes for the session (Claude Code's own tip cooldownSessions pattern, 10 hits in the 2.1.269 binary); `z` snoozes 5 turns, `x` dismisses for the session; at most 1 new nudge per human turn and at most 3 distinct nudges in any 10 human turns (budget stated in turns, not wall-clock, so unattended runs do not starve it); the ctx-price nudge re-fires only at each +100k. Dismissals, snoozes and since_turn persist in ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json with a single writer (the TUI when running, else the CLI/MCP caller) so query/pane/skill rank identically (C062/C064 corrections). SUPPRESSION. session_mode = loop (last 2 stop_hook_summary with hookErrors non-empty or hook_blocking_error hookEvent Stop in the last 3 turns, no typed prompt since), machine (last prompt promptSource system|sdk or origin.kind task-notification) or team (agent-setting lines / stop_hook_summary.teamName) hides every 'reply with…' nudge and shows loop health instead (`Stop hook re-fed the prompt 44× (~210 tok each)`, C058); machine turns are never counted as human turns (C057: 818 heuristic vs 680 promptIds); subagent transcripts never nudge; the first 2 human turns and away > 2 h suppress NEXT/LATER only — NOW alerts (turn died, cache miss, denial) are exempt because 13 of 14 rate-limit errors land on a session's first call (C062 correction); nothing that Claude Code's own footer already says is repeated (`% until auto-compact`, `Context low`, the warm-cache /model confirmation, usage-limit auto-continue; F16). NUMBERS, NOT NAGS. The six tiles always show the problem (a red `cold`, a ×3 turn, a $4.4 vs $0.9 gap); a nudge is added only when a keystroke changes the number, so a person doing one long deliberate task at 500k sees the amber tiles every tick but the checkpoint line at most every +100k. TAPE. The tape is not a nudge channel: it records priced events (≥ 20k tokens or ≥ $0.10 — cache misses with cause, cold writes, agent batches, top-5 % turns, model switches, idle-loop fires, API errors, compactions) newest first, so the person can audit where the money went without being told what to do.
