design:cost-ticker.interaction: TOGGLE. `c` (global, before the '1'-'9' arm in App::handle_key) switches between the 9-panel dashboard and the Ticker; `Esc` in the Ticker returns to the dashboard (matches the overlay/picker convention, VIEW-01). Implemented as `Mode::Coach` passed through layout::solve's `force: Option<Mode>` (C064 correction) rather than a State.view flag, drawn at the top of App::draw (skip the panel layout, render the three frames + footer), persisted in config.toml as `view = \"dashboard\"|\"ticker\"`, selectable with `cctop --view ticker`, and renderable headless with `cctop run --once --keys c --size 56x20` for snapshot tests. `c` is unused today (only Ctrl-C), and every new key is added to BINDINGS so the help-overlay test (app.rs:832-847, FR-11) covers it. NUDGE KEYS. `n` / `N` cycle the ranked candidates (title `1 of 3`; only the slot holder counts as shown); `x` dismisses the current nudge for the session; `z` snoozes it 5 human turns; both toast the rule id like the Advisor does today and persist to ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json. `Enter` = act: reuses the existing `a` ask popup (state.ask, src/ask.rs) pre-filled with the nudge's exact action text — a slash command with its focus filled in (`/compact focus on the auth refactor: keep the test command and open TODOs`), a prompt line (`run cargo test and fix failures before stopping`, `use sonnet for subagents`), or a settings snippet (`\"permissions\": { \"allow\": [\"Bash(gh api:*)\"] }` → localSettings). In the popup Enter copies to the clipboard (ask::copy_to_clipboard) and `S` sends over the session's messaging socket as a peer message (docs/socket.md); slash commands and settings snippets are copy-only and the popup footer says so, because over the socket they would arrive as a message, not a command. `?` (or `e`) opens the why overlay: the rule's explain text (rules::explain, extended for the new ids), the evidence numbers behind the two lines, the priced saving and how it was computed, the acted predicate ('retires when: a test-class Bash call or a Read of an edited file'), the retire-on TTL, and the last 3 retired nudges with their reason (acted / expired / dismissed). `t` toggles the tiles between $ and rate-limit units (subscriber default when rate_limits is present — C005/C024); `↑`/`↓` scroll the tape (50 events kept; `Enter` on a tape row opens the same why overlay for that event, e.g. the cache-miss cause and price); `a` composes an ask from the six tiles (extends ask::compose); `p` pause, `q` quit, `?` help as today. METRICS ↔ TICKER. The dashboard's Advisor panel keeps A01-A18 but shows the Ticker's primary nudge as its first item when the Ticker is not open, so the two never disagree; the dashboard footer gains `c coach`. PANE. In the function-hooks pane the same keys are `Button`s with hotkeys that fire only while the pane is focused (`x`, `z`, `Enter` → `$.prompt.fill` of the action text, never `$.prompt.submit`); `ctrl+x tab` focuses the pane as Claude Code defines it.
design:cost-ticker.delivery_channels: ONE SOURCE. `cctop query coach` (a pure function of State, C064/QUERY-01) returns {state: {word, calls, dctx, verify_age_ms, waiting_on, session_mode}, tiles: [{id, core, suffix, value, unit, metric_id, approx, band}] ×6, nudge: {id, class, line1, line2, action_text, action_kind: slash|prompt|setting|delegate|key, saving, since_turn, retires_on, rank_of}, soon: {id, text, at_ms}, tape: [{at_ms, kind, text, usd, tokens}], suppressed: [ids + reasons]}; the verb truncates line1/line2 to 56 chars and tile cores to 18, so the TUI, the pane and the skill render identically; a `cctop_coach` MCP tool wraps it (one-line addition in src/mcp.rs). TUI TICKER VIEW: everything above — tiles, state line, one nudge + soon, tape, keys. FUNCTION-HOOKS PANE (Overview, plugin/hooks/views/overview.tsx pattern): the poller adds `coach` to its known-verb list and draws the same tree — a header Text (state line, wrap=truncate), a Box grid of 3 rows × 2 tile Boxes at ≥ 60 body columns and 6 stacked rows below (tile core only), a nudge Box with two Text rows + a dim soon row, a tape Box with the last 3 rows; Buttons `x`/`z`/`⏎ act` with hotkeys; colours are palette names only; engine-native figures ($.session.usage() context/rateLimits/cost, turn.step usage for the per-call price and cache-miss toast, agent.spawn/$.agent.list for the agents tile) refresh within 1 s and the binary-backed parts every 2 s busy / 10 s idle (BUSY_POLL_MS/IDLE_POLL_MS). ONE-LINE STATUS ($.ui.status, one per plugin, A05/S01; also `cctop query coach --line` for tmux/shell status bars and the classic renderer): `cctop ≈$0.23/call @412k · warm 41m · turn ≈$2.6 ×3.2 · ▸ agent ac70 398k: use sonnet` truncated to the column width, nudge text dropped first, then the turn multiplier — this is the reduction the brief asks for and it works below 110 columns where the pane is undrawn (S07). TOAST ($.ui.toast 4 s in the pane; the 3-s footer toast in the TUI via alerts.rs deliver()): NOW-class priced events only — cache miss with cause and price (C002), turn died (C060), cold-resume at attach (C026), destructive git on a dirty tree (C044); never NEXT/LATER, never the tiles. PROMPT SUGGEST/FILL (pane only, E08/A06): when the nudge's action_kind is slash or prompt, the `⏎ act` Button calls $.prompt.fill({text}) so the person presses Enter themselves; $.prompt.suggest is used after turn.complete for the `soon` action so Tab accepts it; $.prompt.submit is never called (read-only stance, FR-15). DESKTOP NOTIFICATION (alerts.rs critical() + desktop_notify, opt-in --notify): only `waiting` (AskUserQuestion / permission_prompt / agent_needs_input after 30 s, repeated once at 5 min of cache left) and `turn-died`; the cache-clock joins only when a question or permission is pending, i.e. the person is expected back; Claude Code's own channel gives no desktop toast in tmux/Apple Terminal so this adds value there and duplicates iTerm2's (C042 verdict). EVENTS PANEL: every tape row is also an Event of kind `cost`, so the dashboard's Events panel and `cctop query events` carry the priced history. CCTOP-INSIGHTS SKILL / MCP: the skill's 'why is this session expensive' answer quotes tiles + nudge.line1/line2 + the why text from the same JSON, and because dismissals/first-fire live in ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json (single writer: the TUI while it runs, else the CLI/MCP caller) the skill never contradicts what the person sees; the 2-s pane poller reads that file and never writes it while a TUI is attached. WHY THIS SPLIT: the TUI/pane are the always-on surfaces for numbers (no interruption cost); toasts and desktop alerts are reserved for priced events the person cannot see coming from the numbers (a miss that just happened, a wait they are not aware of); the skill is for the retrospective question, where the same JSON keeps the coach honest.
design:cost-ticker.risks: 1. Shim dependence: the cache tile, the switch-window undo and the exact 5h tile need the status-line shim's prompt_cache / rate_limits (UNS-13, S02); without it the cache tile degrades to `≈warm 1h` from last_line_at_ms + observed_ttl and `5h —`, and the status file is rewritten only when Claude Code redraws or expiry passes, so the countdown must be clock-driven and a stale file (mtime older than the last assistant line) must be ignored (C001). 2. Dollars are notional for subscribers (all 8 status files on this machine carry rate_limits): a $-first ticker can mislead a Max user into optimising a number they do not pay; the `t` toggle must default to limit units when rate_limits is present and the 5h tile must be the headline there (C005/C024); pricing itself is list price and fable-5-1's 0.025× cache read makes the per-call escalation 4× weaker than on opus-5, so per-model prices from pricing.toml, never a rule of thumb. 3. Per-call price is only valid warm; after a TTL flip 1h→5m (3 sessions) or a cold gap the tile must say `(cold: next call ≈$2.0)` or it under-prices the next step by 10-20×. 4. Baseline honesty: baseline.rs medians are per-session (BASE-01); the `×3.2 7d` multiplier needs per-turn medians and ≥ 3 sessions (MIN_TURNS), else the suffix is hidden; a person with one big session in the window sees a meaningless ×. 5. Projection: `next 19c` uses the session's p50 long-run length; early in a session it falls back to the corpus default and can be 1.6× off (C005 verdict refuted the fixed 32); it is labelled ≈ and never drives a nudge alone. 6. Deliberate long context: someone running one long task at 500k on a 1M model will see the ctx-price line at every +100k (3-5 times per such session) — acceptable for a metric, marginal as a nudge; the boundary form must never say 'task done' after a commit alone (19 % precision) and /compact <focus> must lead so nobody /clears mid-task. 7. Synthetic lines: without the C017 filter the ticker would price a $0 turn after a spend-limit error, adopt '<synthetic>' as the model and log a false compaction (8 of 8 corpus 'compactions' are these lines); the filter is a prerequisite, not a nicety. 8. Agents: 66 % of workflow agents here have zero usage (failed spawns); counting them would inflate `agents` and the fan-out nudge — they are excluded and shown as `failed`; async Agent trailers and Workflow results carry no usage, so the tile lags until the agent file is scanned (GAP-01 fix required). 9. Phase word: IMPLEMENTING/EXPLORING from tool names is reliable, VERIFYING is not (47-56 % agreement for write+run Bash, C041/C055); the state line therefore shows the literal check (`✓ cargo test 3m ago`) rather than an inferred VERIFYING, and the no-check nudge stays silent when the test class is unknown — the ~200-call hand-label pass is a gate before it escalates. 10. Turn identity: the current heuristic over-counts human turns by 20 % (818 vs 680 promptIds, C057); cooldowns and budgets counted in 'human turns' inherit that error until promptSource/origin.kind are parsed. 11. Nudge fatigue and wrong retirement: acted predicates can misfire (an Agent spawned for another reason retires the explore nudge; a Read of an edited file counts as a check) — mitigated by also retiring on predicate-false and by the 3-shown self-snooze; conversely cooldowns can hide a genuinely repeated problem, which is why the tiles keep showing it. 12. Bot loops and machine turns: without the session_mode gate the coach fires 'reply with…' into an unattended Ralph terminal (44 iterations in one session) and prices task-notification turns as human turns; the gate relies on stop_hook_summary.hookErrors / promptSource shapes that are version-specific (2.1.220+). 13. Post-hoc switch detection: history.jsonl rows land after the switch executed, so without the PreModelSwitch hook the switch-window nudge is an undo window that competes with Claude Code's own warm-cache confirmation dialog (F16); it may read as redundant and is P2 for that reason. 14. Three surfaces, one state file: the 2-s pane poller, a CLI/MCP caller and the TUI can race on ~/.cctop/<session>.advisor.json; the single-writer rule (TUI owns it while attached) must be enforced or since_turn/dismissals diverge and the pane shows a nudge the TUI retired. 15. Width: every line is designed for 56 and truncated by the verb; at 40 columns tile suffixes and the tape disappear, and a nudge line cut at 38 chars can lose its action — the line2 text is composed action-first for that reason. 16. Tape noise: priced events below 20k tokens / $0.10 are dropped, but a screenshot-heavy or loop-heavy session can still fill it; it scrolls and never takes the nudge slot. 17. Wording promises: 'queue it now' lands at turn end (26/28), '/compact pays ~half' is an estimate of one cold read, 'saves ≈3× per agent call' assumes sonnet at the same tool count — each why overlay states the assumption so the person can judge it.
